proposals.name: Nottawa Community School Bond Proposal
proposals.description:
Shall Nottawa Community School, St. Joseph County, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Four Million Three Hundred Sixty Thousand Dollars ($4,360,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, for the purpose of:
erecting, furnishing, and equipping additions to school buildings and the Nottawa Stone School; remodeling, furnishing and refurnishing, and equipping and re-equipping school buildings and the Nottawa Stone School; and preparing, developing, improving, and…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall Nottawa Community School, St. Joseph County, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Four Million Three Hundred Sixty Thousand Dollars ($4,360,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, for the purpose of:
erecting, furnishing, and equipping additions to school buildings and the Nottawa Stone School; remodeling, furnishing and refurnishing, and equipping and re-equipping school buildings and the Nottawa Stone School; and preparing, developing, improving, and equipping drop-off areas, driveways, parking lots, playgrounds, and sites?
The following is for informational purposes only:
The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027 is 2.53 mills ($2.53 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation). The maximum number of years the bonds may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is twenty-five (25) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is 1.95 mills ($1.95 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).
(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote authorizes the sale of $4.36 million in bonds, repaid through a property tax levy over the life of the bonds.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the borrowing — no bonds are issued and no new debt levy is added.
proposals.conservativeView: Bonds commit taxpayers to decades of debt service. Ask whether the project list is needs or wants, whether the district has maintained what it already has, and what the total interest cost will be. "No tax rate increase" often means extending an existing levy for many more years rather than letting it expire.
proposals.progressiveView: Bonds let communities fund major facility needs — safety, infrastructure, aging buildings — spreading the cost over the years the improvements will be used.

proposals.name: White Pigeon Community Schools Sinking Fund Millage Replacement Proposal
proposals.description:
This proposal will allow the school district to replace the building and site sinking fund millage previously approved by the electors.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in White Pigeon Community Schools, St. Joseph and Cass Counties, Michigan, be increased by and the board of education be authorized to levy not to exceed 3 mills ($3.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 5 years, 2027 to 2031, inclusive, to replace the…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to replace the building and site sinking fund millage previously approved by the electors.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in White Pigeon Community Schools, St. Joseph and Cass Counties, Michigan, be increased by and the board of education be authorized to levy not to exceed 3 mills ($3.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 5 years, 2027 to 2031, inclusive, to replace the previously approved sinking fund millage with a sinking fund millage for the purchase of real estate for sites for, and the construction or repair of, school buildings; for school security improvements; for the acquisition or upgrading of technology; for the acquisition of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used for the maintenance of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of eligible trucks and vans used to carry parts, equipment, and personnel for or in the maintenance of school buildings; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used to maintain such trucks and vans; and for all other purposes authorized by law; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $1,808,420 (this is a replacement of millage that expires with the 2026 tax levy)?
proposals.officialTitle: WHITE PIGEON COMMUNITY SCHOOLS SINKING FUND MILLAGE REPLACEMENT PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote approves a new levy of 3 mills for 5 years — this is a tax increase.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the new tax; your property tax rate stays where it is.
proposals.conservativeView: This is new taxation. Ask whether the need could be met within existing budgets, whether the millage sunsets, and who oversees how the money is spent.
proposals.progressiveView: New funding dedicated to a specific local service that supporters say current revenue cannot cover.

proposals.name: Mottville Township Prohibition of Marihuana Establishments Ordinance
proposals.description:
IT IS HEREBY ORDAINED BY THE PEOPLE OF MOTTVILLE TOWNSHIP THAT:
Section 1. The title of this ordinance shall be the “Mottville Township Prohibition of Marihuana Establishments Ordinance.”
Section 2. Marihuana Establishments Prohibited. Marihuana establishments, as defined by MCL 333.27953(l), are prohibited within the boundaries of Mottville Township.
Shall the “The Mottville Township Prohibition of Marihuana Establishments Ordinance” be approved?

proposals.name: Nottawa Community School Bond Proposal
proposals.description:
Shall Nottawa Community School, St. Joseph County, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Four Million Three Hundred Sixty Thousand Dollars ($4,360,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, for the purpose of:
erecting, furnishing, and equipping additions to school buildings and the Nottawa Stone School; remodeling, furnishing and refurnishing, and equipping and re-equipping school buildings and the Nottawa Stone School; and preparing, developing, improving, and…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall Nottawa Community School, St. Joseph County, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Four Million Three Hundred Sixty Thousand Dollars ($4,360,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, for the purpose of:
erecting, furnishing, and equipping additions to school buildings and the Nottawa Stone School; remodeling, furnishing and refurnishing, and equipping and re-equipping school buildings and the Nottawa Stone School; and preparing, developing, improving, and equipping drop-off areas, driveways, parking lots, playgrounds, and sites?
The following is for informational purposes only:
The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027 is 2.53 mills ($2.53 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation). The maximum number of years the bonds may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is twenty-five (25) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is 1.95 mills ($1.95 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).
(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote authorizes the sale of $4.36 million in bonds, repaid through a property tax levy over the life of the bonds.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the borrowing — no bonds are issued and no new debt levy is added.
proposals.conservativeView: Bonds commit taxpayers to decades of debt service. Ask whether the project list is needs or wants, whether the district has maintained what it already has, and what the total interest cost will be. "No tax rate increase" often means extending an existing levy for many more years rather than letting it expire.
proposals.progressiveView: Bonds let communities fund major facility needs — safety, infrastructure, aging buildings — spreading the cost over the years the improvements will be used.

proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to replace the building and site sinking fund millage previously approved by the electors.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in White Pigeon Community Schools, St. Joseph and Cass Counties, Michigan, be increased by and the board of education be authorized to levy not to exceed 3 mills ($3.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 5 years, 2027 to 2031, inclusive, to replace the previously approved sinking fund millage with a sinking fund millage for the purchase of real estate for sites for, and the construction or repair of, school buildings; for school security improvements; for the acquisition or upgrading of technology; for the acquisition of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used for the maintenance of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of eligible trucks and vans used to carry parts, equipment, and personnel for or in the maintenance of school buildings; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used to maintain such trucks and vans; and for all other purposes authorized by law; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $1,808,420 (this is a replacement of millage that expires with the 2026 tax levy)?
proposals.officialTitle: WHITE PIGEON COMMUNITY SCHOOLS SINKING FUND MILLAGE REPLACEMENT PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote approves a new levy of 3 mills for 5 years — this is a tax increase.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the new tax; your property tax rate stays where it is.
proposals.conservativeView: This is new taxation. Ask whether the need could be met within existing budgets, whether the millage sunsets, and who oversees how the money is spent.
proposals.progressiveView: New funding dedicated to a specific local service that supporters say current revenue cannot cover.
